sections.COMMENTS:
ï»¿    **COMMENTS**
This Source is based on geological data of the Colli Albani Volcanic Complex (e.g. De Rita et al., 1988, 1995a) constrained by the occurrence of the 26 August 1806 earthquake (Me 5.6), whose epicentral area is located in the Colli Albani area, including the towns of Rocca di Papa, Nemi and Velletri, ca. 25 km south of Rome.
This Source is a NW-dipping normal fault. It roots within the carbonatic and terrigenous bedrock, below the 1.5-3 km depth range of the volcanic cover (Funiciello and Parotto, 1978).
The Colli Albani Volcano became active at ca. 600 Ky, and that belongs to the roman magmatic province in the Tyrrhenian coastal region. Present-day activity consists of frequent shallow earthquake swarms (Chiarabba et al., 1994), and peculiar gas emissions (Pizzino et al., 2002; Carapezza et al., 2003).  The Colli Albani Volcano has been classified as quiescent (De Rita et al., 1995b), on the basis of the recurrence time of eruptions (10 ky) comparable with the elapsed time since the last eruption (25 ky BP; Voltaggio and Barbieri, 1995; Funiciello et al., 2003; De Benedetti et al., 2008).
The seismicity linked to the volcanic processes is characterized by low magnitude events (the maximum magnitude seldom exceeds Ml 4.0), shallow epicenters (less than 7 km depth), and normal or subordinately strike-slip faulting mechanisms (Amato and Chiarabba, 1995a, 1995b). The frequent seismic swarms are random series of small earthquakes, without a clear mainshock-aftershock sequence as generally observed in tectonic environment, and during the 1806 seismic events (Spadea et al., 1985).
The location, geometry and strike of this Source is chosen according to the main NE-SW oriented fault system in the Colli Albani Complex area (De Rita et al., 1988; Faccenna et al., 1994; De Rita et al., 1995a; Giordano et al., 2006), and to the main structural pattern, inferred from morphological evidence, straddling the area from Lanuvio to Stazione di Palestrina (Caputo et al., 1995).
The strike of this Source follows the master fault known in the literature and the 45km-long lineament recognised by Caputo et al. (1995).
The fault dips to the northwest, according to geological data, and is consistent with the inversion of the gravimetric profile (Di Filippo and Toro, 1995).
The rake is assumed to be pure normal faulting, inferred from the strain analyses that indicate a N40Â°W oriented local extensional stress (Sagnotti et al., 1994). Length and width are obtained from scaling relationships, constrained by the 1806 earthquake magnitude.
The epicentral zone and maximum intensity of the 1806 Me 5.6 earthquake are well constrained by the abundant documentation regarding the town of Velletri, that have led to assign a maximum MCS intensity of VIII to this event (Boschi et al., 2000; Spadea et al., 1985). The analysis of the macroseismic data reveals that (a) the epicentral zone includes a rather large area of the Colli Albani, and (b) the event affected a very large region, with III degree detected as far away as Naples (Spadea et al., 1985).
The proposed depth of this Source is inferred from the extents and pattern of the damage area caused by the 1806 earthquake.
sections.OPEN QUESTIONS:
1) What is the average recurrence interval of this Source?
2) What are the relationships between the shallow Colli Albani volcanic events and the 1806 event at depth?
3) Can this Source represent an important hazard for the very close city of Rome?

pictures.t: Geologic map of Quaternary volcanic complex of Colli Albani
pictures.c: Geologic map of Quaternary volcanic complex of Colli Albani (Anzidei et al. [1998]). The Velletri seismogenic source lies on a NE-SW trending normal fault on the SW side of the complex and its activity is related to nomal faulting in horst-graben system of the central Tyrrhenian sea margin.

pictures.t: Map of gravimetric Bouguer anomalies in the Colli Albani area
pictures.c: Gravimetric Bouguer anomalies on the Digital Elevation Model of the volcano show the relationships between the deep structure and the main morphological lineaments. Colli Albani volcanic system is located in a region characterized by the convergence of positive and negative gravity axis. These data suggest that the basement is highly fractured and dislocated in a horst and graben like style (Giordano et al. [2006]).

pictures.t: Structural block diagram of the Colli Albani vulcanic system
pictures.c: Interpretative block diagram of the volcano-tectonic structure of the caldera of the Colli Albani. Vulcanic activity is strongly related to the present horst and graben rift system at deeper parts of the crust. Fault dips are consistent with the inversion of the gravimetric profile. The NE-trending Artemisio fissure corresponds to the master fault of the Ardea basin, as interpreted from offshore seismic profiles (Giordano et al.[2006]).
